original_value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative movement disorder where motor dysfunction gradually increases. PD-specific dopaminergic drugs can ameliorate symptoms, but neurologists also strongly recommend physiotherapy combined with regular exercise. As there is no known cure for PD, traditional rehabilitation programs eventually tire and bore patients to the point of losing interest and dropping out of those programs just because of the predictability and repeatability of the exercises. This can be avoided with the help of current technology, character-based, interactive 3D games promote physical training in a nonlinear fashion, and can provide experiences that change each time the game is played. Such “exergames” (a combination of the words “exercise” and “game”) challenge patients into performing exercises of varying complexity in a playful and interactive environment. In this work we present a Unity3D-based platform hosting two exergames tailored to PD patients with mild to moderate symptoms. The platform employs Microsoft Kinect, an affordable off-the-shelf motion capture sensor that can be easily installed in both home and clinical settings. Platform navigation and gameplay rely on a collection of gestures specifically developed for this purpose and are based upon training programs tailored to PD. These gestures employ purposeful, large-amplitude movements intended to improve postural stability and reflexes and increase upper and lower limb mobility. When the patient’s movements, as detected by Kinect, “match” a preprogrammed gesture, an onscreen 3D cartoon avatar responds according to the game context at hand. In addition, ingame decision-making aims at improving cognitive reaction.

result.paraphrase: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative movement disorder in which motor impairment steadily worsens. PD-specific dopaminergic medications can relieve symptoms, but neurologists also strongly advise physiotherapy together with regular exercise. Because there is no known cure for PD, conventional rehabilitation programs often eventually make patients tired and bored, leading them to lose interest and drop out due to the predictability and repetition of the exercises. Current technology can help prevent this: character-driven, interactive 3D games support physical training in a nonlinear way and can offer experiences that vary each time they are played. Such “exergames” (from “exercise” and “game”) encourage patients to perform exercises of different difficulty in a playful, interactive setting. In this work, we present a Unity3D-based platform that hosts two exergames designed for PD patients with mild to moderate symptoms. The platform uses Microsoft Kinect, an affordable off-the-shelf motion capture sensor that can be installed easily in both home and clinical environments. Navigation and gameplay are based on a set of gestures developed specifically for this purpose and grounded in PD-tailored training programs. These gestures use deliberate, large-amplitude movements meant to improve postural stability and reflexes and to increase upper and lower limb mobility. When Kinect detects that the patient’s movements “match” a preprogrammed gesture, an onscreen 3D cartoon avatar reacts according to the current game context. In addition, in-game decision-making is intended to improve cognitive reaction.
